name: html-class-sized-image-auto-width-carrier
description: The be-inline-geometry carrier for a class-sized (fixed height + `width:auto` + a max-width clamp, e.g. Tailwind's `h-10 w-auto max-w-[200px]`) must restate the author's `width:auto` explicitly alongside `max-width`, not just `max-width` alone. WordPress core's own block-library stylesheet declares a DIFFERENT default for the free `width` axis of `.wp-block-image img` in each rendering context -- `width:auto` on the frontend (which happens to match the author) but `width:100%` in the editor canvas (which does not) -- so a carrier that states only `max-width` leaves the editor canvas to stretch the image to that clamp instead of deriving it from the fixed height and the image's real aspect ratio. Also covers a sibling image sized by an explicit `w-8` (no `auto`) to prove that image is unaffected: it keeps carrying only its own box constraints, with no `width:auto` added.

source_reference.notes: Regression coverage for the editor-canvas-only stretch completing #1933: ImageDimensionResolver::authorResolvesDimensionToAuto() already detects an author-stated `auto` to suppress the intrinsic width attribute; StyleResolver::imageBoxConstraintClassName() now reuses that same detection to also state `width:auto` on the be-inline-geometry carrier.

legacy_comparison.reason: This upstream primitive fixture has no downstream legacy comparison.
